seoTitle: Tone of Voice Analyzer: Formality, Confidence, Urgency
metaDescription: Score text for formality, confidence, urgency, positivity and directness with word lists and sentence statistics. English, runs locally.
intro: Check how your copy sounds: formal or casual, confident or hedging, urgent or calm, and whether it speaks to the reader.
why:
Five dimensions are scored 0-100 from counts of formal and casual words, hedges and certainty words, urgency phrases, positive and negative words, second-person pronouns, exclamation marks, contractions, questions and average sentence length. The detail lines show the raw counts so you can see why a score came out as it did.

This is a lexicon method, so sarcasm, jargon and non-English text are misread. It is best for comparing two drafts of the same piece or checking that a brand voice guide is followed, not for judging a person.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Paste at least a paragraph of English text.
Read the five scores and the matched-word counts.
Edit the draft and run it again to compare.
Keep the tone that fits your audience.

faq.a: No. It uses fixed word lists and punctuation counts.

faq.q: What is a good formality score?
faq.a: It depends on the audience: legal copy scores high, social posts low. Compare against your own examples.

faq.q: Why is my score low on confidence?
faq.a: Words like maybe, perhaps and might lower it; words like always, will and guarantee raise it.
